title: Gold relationship
description: A known relationship, with the verbatim sentence that states it. Shape only.

predicate.description: From the approved relationship dictionary. NOT enumerated here: the dictionary is expert-owned and does not exist yet, and an agent listing plausible predicates would be authoring the vocabulary the dictionary is supposed to fix (CLAUDE.md rule 1). When the dictionary lands, this becomes an enum generated from it.

modality.description: must | may | should, where the relation is normative. Null means not yet supplied, and is reported as a gap — never inferred from the sentence's grammar, because whether a 'may' is possibility or permission is a legal reading (guide §5.4, P8).

applies_when.description: The condition under which the supporting sentence states the relationship, copied from that sentence and never retyped: 'an application to record assignment is received after …'. The antecedent only; how strongly the sentence states it is `hedge`. Optional; absent means no condition was recorded. Shown wherever the edge is shown, so an edge never reads as more than its sentence says (the review response, F14; the second response, R01).

hedge.description: How strongly the supporting sentence states the relationship, its own strength word or phrase copied verbatim: 'usually', 'rarely', 'Generally', 'not likely'. Split from applies_when in S041, where five records held a hedge or an outcome in place of a condition (the second review response, R01). Optional; absent means the sentence states it without one.

no_condition.description: Why the conditional marker in the supporting sentence ('if', 'where', 'unless', 'when', 'except') does not condition this relationship: the reader's judgement, so the record reads as assessed rather than not assessed (the second review response, R07; ontology.conditions). Never beside applies_when.
